handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer_position is above 0.26. The earliest represented state intentionally has red still held or touching down at the outside pad, fingers closed, and blue resting outside; after red release, the TCP is free to retreat and acquire blue. Red is predecessor-release context, while blue is the intended object.
handoff.exit_conditions: At one observation, drawer_position is strictly above 0.26, the red block is fully contained on the outside pad with center z in (0.014,0.031), and the blue block is fully contained in the open drawer cavity with center z in (0.053,0.074). Demonstrations additionally show open fingers and a high retreat, but those are retained transition context rather than added success requirements.
handoff.failure_signatures: Red moves off the pad during retreat; TCP approaches the predecessor red instead of blue; gripper closes without blue/TCP co-motion; blue is carried into drawer walls or lip; drawer_position falls to 0.26 or below; blue center/rotated extent is not fully inside the cavity; blue z is outside (0.053,0.074); or final red containment is lost. Demonstrations do not show recovery from these failures.
handoff.overlap_role: With red_transfer, shared actions are 600:850 in every trajectory: 250 supervised actions per occurrence, 3,000 total, lasting 12.5 s per occurrence. They include final red lowering while still grasped, red release, retreat, cross-scene transit, blue approach/descent/contact, gripper closure, and blue lift. This supplies the receiving skill with action labels across the object-identity change and a wide range of switch times.
handoff.successor_readiness: There is no further learned manipulation successor. Readiness for framework success evaluation is the unchanged simultaneous completion expression: drawer_open AND red_on_pad AND blue_inside. The final high retreat is observed but is not required by that evaluator.

name: Pick the blue block and place it inside the open drawer
segmentation_rationale: Blue pickup, long transport, and confined placement into the drawer cavity form a separate responsibility from placing red on an open pad. Each start boundary was separately checked at the red-pad contact state, and each stop is that trajectory's final observation/action boundary. The full demonstrated release and high retreat are retained even though gripper release and TCP clearance are not evaluator requirements.

subgoal: Primary responsibility: finish the predecessor red release/retreat context, acquire the blue block outside the drawer, lift and transport it to the open drawer cavity, lower it inside, release it, and retreat to a high clear pose. The intended object is blue; the red block visible at segment entry is only the predecessor object still being lowered/released. Observed contact/motion: at observation 600 red is still pinched near the pad at z about 0.032-0.037 m; by 700 red is settled at z about 0.020 m and the open gripper is retreating toward blue; around 800 the TCP descends over blue; by 850 blue is pinched and lifted; later it is carried to the drawer, lowered to z about 0.063 m, released, and the TCP retreats to z about 0.323 m. Final observations in all occurrences simultaneously show drawer_position about 0.297, red near (-0.176 to -0.177,-0.298 to -0.304,0.020), and blue near (-0.171 to -0.173,0.073 to 0.074,0.063), satisfying the supplied one-observation completion rule. The demo1000 final front image supports blue in the drawer, red on the outside pad, and the open drawer. Purpose/expected benefit: retaining the long release-to-pick overlap should make this independently trained insertion model usable from intermediate transition states; demonstrated success does not establish recovery from dropped blue blocks, drawer collisions, or unseen placements.
